stories.title: Search continues after deadly mine collapse on Cameroon-Central African Republic border
stories.summary: In tonight’s edition: a deadly landslide at a gold mine in the Central African Republic leaves dozens dead, with victims from Cameroon and Chad. Meanwhile, Ethiopia is turning to Bordeaux expertise and grapevines in a bid to become East Africa’s next wine destination. Finally, Belgium continues to confront its colonial past, more than a century after Congolese people were displayed at the 1894 Antwerp World’s Fair.

stories.title: Outrage in India over death of six-year-old ‘slapped’ by his teacher
stories.summary: Andhra Pradesh’s regional minister of education says he is taking legal action with a committee against those responsible. Authorities in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh have launched an investigation after a six-year-old child collapsed and reportedly died after he was slapped by his teacher in a school classroom. The incident was captured on a security camera in the school in Visakhapatnam in the southeast Indian state, before being shared widely by local media on Thursday. The incident is already causing an uproar around corporal punishment in the country. The video clip, which has been verified by Al Jazeera, shows a female teacher holding a child by his clothes before slapping him on the face, after which he collapses. “We are taking legal action against those responsible and the school management,” Nara Lokesh, Andhra Pradesh’s education and IT minister, wrote on Facebook on Thursday. Police are also investigating the circumstances around the death of the child, who local media have named as Pranay Tej. “As a father, I can’t get over what happened to little Pranay Tej. I cannot imagine the pain his parents are going through. Corporal punishment has no place in our schools. No child should ever be subjected to violence in the name of discipline,” Lokesh wrote on X on Friday. “I have already directed a full investigation and strict action against anyone found responsible.

stories.title: Georgia declines to join new EU sanctions against Iran
stories.summary: Georgia declines to join new EU sanctions against Iran Georgia has declined to join the European Union’s latest sanctions against Iran, saying its foreign policy decisions are guided by national interests, Iran’s state news agency, IRNA, reported. stories.title: How this 1960s ex-council house is managing to stay cool without air con
stories.summary: After five heatwaves and plenty of advice on how to stay safe in what is set to become the UK's hottest summer on record, many people continue to find it a challenge to stay cool - particularly in their homes. This is perhaps no surprise. More than half of homes, external in the UK are already at risk of overheating and at current rates of climate change this will rise to 92% by 2050 if we do not adapt. But in south London, on a 35C day, one 1960s ex-council house, with no air-conditioning is managing to stay remarkably cool. Marion Baeli's home is one of many across the UK being adapted for warmer - maybe even 40C - British summers. As well as being the homeowner, Baeli is an architect - and she compares her house to a well-insulated flask. "You wouldn't put holes in your flask if you wanted to keep the ice in. You'd close the cap and make sure it is firmly twisted on. It's the same in this house." When the BBC visit Baeli on the hottest day of this summer's fourth heatwave, her house is 10C cooler than outside. "It feels like you have air-conditioning [inside the house] but you haven't. This is the beauty of the Passivhaus standard," she explains.
